2027-01-10.title: The Baptism of the Lord · Feast
readings: Here is my servant, in whom my soul delights
The Lord will bless his people with peace
God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and with power
You are my Son, the Beloved
2027-01-10.alt: Year B alternatives: Isaiah 55:1–11; Isaiah 12; 1 John 5:1–9. The Christmas season ends today; Ordinary Time begins tomorrow. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-10.verse: And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
theo: The Christmas season closes at the river Jordan. Mark tells it with few words and great force. John proclaims: “The one who is more powerful than I is coming after me… I have baptized you with water; but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.” Then Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptised. As he comes up out of the water, “he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.” The Father speaks: “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”

Isaiah had described this Servant: “Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him.” He will not shout or break a bruised reed; he will bring justice and be “a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind.” In Acts, Peter tells the household of Cornelius how “God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil.” The anointing at the Jordan is the beginning of the Christ's public mission, and Peter's sermon shows it reaching the Gentiles.

Jesus had no sin to wash away. He went down into the water in solidarity with sinners and to sanctify the waters for our Baptism (CCC 536, 1224). What the Father said to Jesus, he says to each of us in Baptism: you are my beloved child. The torn heavens are not closed again; through Christ, heaven is open to us. Today is a good day to renew our baptismal promises and to live as people anointed by the Spirit for doing good.
conn: Mark uses the strong verb schizō: the heavens are “torn apart”. He uses it again only once, for the Temple curtain at Jesus' death (Mark 15:38). The way to God is opened at the Jordan and at Calvary.
Isaiah 42:1–4 is the first of four Servant Songs (Isaiah 42, 49, 50, 52–53). The Father's words at the Jordan echo Isaiah 42:1 and Psalm 2:7.
The Spirit hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2) and the dove returning to Noah's ark (Genesis 8:11) stand behind this sign: a new creation begins.
Peter's sermon in Acts 10 is preached to a Roman centurion's household. The Spirit falls on Gentiles, and they are baptised: the Jordan's grace reaches the nations.
“Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew) mean Anointed. At the Jordan Jesus is anointed with the Spirit for his mission (Acts 10:38; CCC 438).
The Christmas season ends with this feast. Tomorrow the Church begins Ordinary Time, following the public life of Jesus Sunday by Sunday.
altar: At the Jordan the Spirit came down on Jesus. At the altar the priest calls down the same Spirit on the bread and wine (the epiclesis), and they become the Body and Blood of Christ.
Our Baptism made us members of Christ's Body; the Eucharist nourishes that life. Font and altar belong together.

Isaiah's gentle Servant, a light to the nations.
The Spirit and the Father's voice.
What the Father says to us.

live: At Mass today renew your baptismal promises with full attention; at home, light your baptismal candle if you have it.
Ask your parents or parish and write the date in your diary.
Like Jesus who went about doing good, do one deliberate act of kindness each day this week.
Bless yourself with holy water when you enter and leave church.
fathers: Christ is bathed in light; let us also be bathed in light. Christ is baptised; let us also go down with him, that we may also rise with him.
Christ is baptised not to be made holy by the water, but to make the water holy.
magis: Christ's Baptism and the Church's Baptism.
Know the date of your Baptism and celebrate it.
saints: 13 Jan: St Hilary. 14 Jan: St Devasahayam (in India). 17 Jan: St Antony, abbot (Sunday this year).
2027-01-10.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, who, when Christ had been baptised in the River Jordan and as the Holy Spirit descended upon him, solemnly declared him your beloved Son, grant that your children by adoption, reborn of water and the Holy Spirit, may always be well pleasing to you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

illus: A parish in Kollam started a simple custom: every child receives a card with the date of their Baptism, and on that day the family lights the baptismal candle at supper. A teacher said her pupils now know their baptism days as well as their birthdays, and some insist on going to Mass that day.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at the Jordan the heavens opened and the Father called you his beloved Son. Open heaven over us as we gather, and renew in us the grace of our Baptism. Amen.
share: “Here is my servant… I have put my spirit upon him” (Isaiah 42:1). How does the Spirit work in me?
“God anointed Jesus… he went about doing good” (Acts 10:38). What good can I do this week?
“You are my Son, the Beloved” (Mark 1:11). Do I believe God says this to me?
pm.resp: Lord, renew in us the grace of Baptism.
interc: For all the baptised, that they may live as children of God.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism at Easter.
For parents and godparents, that they may hand on the faith.
For those who have drifted from the faith received in Baptism.
For our group, that we may go about doing good like Jesus.
pm.close: Father, at the Jordan you anointed your Son with the Spirit. Keep us faithful to our Baptism, and send us out to do good in his name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the Christmas season ends at the river Jordan. Mark tells the story in a few lines. John the Baptist says: the one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit (Mark 1:7–8).

Then Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptised. As he comes up out of the water, he sees the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice from heaven says: you are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased (Mark 1:10–11). Father, Son and Holy Spirit are revealed together.

Isaiah described this Servant long before: here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him (Isaiah 42:1). He will not break a bruised reed. He will be a light to the nations and open the eyes of the blind.

In the second reading Peter sums up Jesus' whole life in one sentence: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil (Acts 10:38). That anointing began at the Jordan. And Peter says this to a Roman family: the grace of the Jordan is for every nation.
Why was the sinless Jesus baptised? To stand with sinners and to make the waters holy for us. In our Baptism the heavens opened over us too, and the Father said: you are my beloved child.
So today let us renew our baptismal promises with all our heart. Let us find out the date of our Baptism. And let us go about doing good this week, as people anointed by the Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus was baptised in the river. The Holy Spirit came like a dove and God said: you are my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents to show you your Baptism photos!

homily: Dear friends, long ago Isaiah cried out: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1). Israel longed for God to come close. At the Jordan the prayer is answered: as Jesus came up from the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him (Mark 1:10).

This is the great manifestation of the Trinity. The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father's voice says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:17). Every time we make the sign of the cross, we confess what was revealed at the Jordan.
Jesus did not need to be cleansed. The Fathers said: he went into the water not to be made holy by it, but to make the waters holy for us. From that day, water became the doorway into God's life.

Paul says: he saved us through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). What happened at the Jordan happened to us at the font. Heaven opened over us; the Father called us his children.
Today let us thank God for our Baptism, make the sign of the cross with faith, and come to the Mass as children of an open heaven. Amen.

opts.resolve: This week I will find my Baptism date, thank my godparents, and renew my baptismal promises.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, most of us were baptised as infants. We do not remember the water, the oil or the candle. Today, as we celebrate the Lord's own baptism, the Church invites us to remember what God did to us.

Paul asks: do you not know that all of us who have been baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death? We were buried with him by baptism, so that we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3–4). The font is both a tomb and a womb.

He also says: as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). That is why we received a white garment. We are called to wear Christ every day, at home, at work, in our words.

At Baptism a candle was lit for us, and our godparents spoke promises on our behalf: to reject sin and to believe. Now that we are grown, those promises are ours to keep. Once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light (Ephesians 5:8).
So let us find the date of our Baptism, thank our godparents, and tonight renew our promises: I reject sin; I believe in God. Then come to the Mass as children of the light. Amen.
